name: Claudius Lysius
overview: Claudius Lysius, identified as the chief captain of the Roman band, plays a crucial role in the protection and custody of the Apostle Paul during a time of intense hostility in Jerusalem. The sample verses depict Lysius responding to a violent uproar against Paul by intervening decisively to prevent his harm, commanding soldiers to rescue him from a threatening mob and ultimately sending him to the governor Felix for a formal hearing. These actions highlight Lysius as a Roman military officer entrusted with maintaining order and facilitating the legal process amid the early church's challenges.
